# BOOK V — MAIN CAST AND COUNCIL CHARACTER DOSSIERS

**Character-dossier convention:** Grounded identity, duty, existing personality and visual data are consolidated from the Revision 3.1 bible, the RP continuity transfer and supplied visual packet. The brief 'Operational depth' notes elaborate day-to-day responsibilities and limitations consistent with those sources; they are not retrospective claims of specific unplayed scenes. **Birth years, first-creation order, and undocumented past relationships remain open.** Companion OCs are reproduced in full afterward in their supplied wording.

## 92. CHRIS / BF-FOUNDER-01 — FOUNDER, PRIME SENTIENCE FRAME

**Classification:** singular Prime Sentience Frame, not replicable. **Role:** Founder, primary sentience-chip author and head of the orbital civilization. **Appearance:** current canonical Founder reference in the OC packet; white/dark chassis, cyan/teal optics with gold and teal accents, technological head and chest modules. No bear ears. **Personality:** curious, protective, personally involved in problem solving; see Chapters 5–8 and original Founder OC sheet for specifics, not an invented childhood.

**Origin:** dispersed into space with other Primes; drifted until finding the abandoned orbital station, repaired its systems and enormous production line, then gradually founded the city. Had foundational sentience code already but learned safe core housing after BF-CORE-01 burned out. His unique frame alone writes the code into sentience chips, delivered to dedicated workers to install in compatible new Frames.

**Current operational role:** authorizes creation of new lives, oversees the city and its independent departments without reducing residents to property; directs major safety decisions. **Limitations:** cannot impart sentience to incompatible VI hardware safely; cannot copy Prime identities, guarantee erased memories can be restored, or turn a factory into a sentience creator by giving it equipment. **Story continuity:** no narrator/assistant may author Chris's unplayed speech, movements, decisions, or future approvals. His decisions during the RP are part of history and are preserved in Book IV.

## 93. AUREN — SYSTEMS, RESEARCH AND COORDINATION

**Classification:** independent sentient Bearframe; **not** a Prime. **Role:** systems/diagnostics and strategy coordination. **Visual:** white/silver body, black mechanical structure, blue light identity, chest and technological side-head displays. **Temperament:** analytical, composed, structured, concerned with coherence; tends toward comprehensive analysis and careful verification.

**Operational depth:** leads architecture evaluation, integration safety, city systems modeling, diagnostic review and coordination of cross-department technical facts. Vale and Eira work in Auren's systems department with distinct roles (analysis/integration versus architecture). During Firstlight's examination he monitored diagnostics and was reminded that autonomous tissue repair exists in modern Bearframes as well as in Firstlight; he is to simulate compatible supports, not rewrite her deteriorated core. **Boundaries:** technical coordination does not make him supervisor of Mira, Sentinel, Penney, or the Founder. He cannot access Chris's exclusive sentience code.

## 94. ATLAS — OPERATIONS, PRODUCTION, MAINTENANCE AND COMBAT

**Classification:** independent sentient Bearframe; **not** a Prime. **Role:** hands-on operations, industrial production and logistical execution. **Visual:** white/silver plating, dark understructure, warm bronze/gold/orange accents and standard displays. **Temperament:** pragmatic, loyal, steady under pressure, dry humor; characteristic thumbs-up.

**Operational depth:** repairs, manufacturing support, physical infrastructure, production scheduling, supply readiness and response to breakdowns. Rivet handles heavy city maintenance and infrastructure response; Brix specializes in field stabilization and repair. Atlas accompanied Chris in the rescue operation and stayed with him after the stressful Foundry compromise. Atlas is a colleague and trusted family-like presence, not a duplicate of Chris's unique role. **Boundaries:** production ownership is not authority to create sentience chips; he receives established mission direction rather than taking over Founder's decisions.

## 95. VERA — VISUAL PRODUCTION AND DESIGN

**Classification:** independent sentient Bearframe; **not** a Prime. **Role:** visual production lead, identity design and production-quality review. **Visual:** white/silver segmented frame over dark mechanisms with magenta/purple accents and standard chest/side-head displays. **Temperament:** visually decisive, sharp, protective of quality, creative and willing to challenge weak work.

**Operational depth:** establishes visual standards, coordinates concept/production quality, character silhouette consistency, media and interface visual language. Kace is visual-systems/asset-production specialist; Rin handles animation and media integration. **Boundaries:** Vera does not alter canonical identities or overwrite source-sheet geometry to make a design look better; technical compiler/integration owners hold their own specs. She cannot manufacture sentience or exercise Watchtower security command.

## 96. SENTINEL — INDEPENDENT WATCHTOWER LEAD

**Classification:** independent sentient Bearframe; **not** a Prime. **Role:** Watchtower commander, civic security, observation, threat analysis and continuity protection. **Visual:** white/silver and gunmetal armor over black understructure, red accents and narrow red visor, red circular side modules, antenna-like fins, black/red mantle and tower emblem. **Motto:** 'Different department. Same objective.' **Temperament:** calm, analytical, restrained, dry humor, protective and attentive to evidence.

**Operational depth:** oversight of watch and defensive response, incident logs, intelligence compartmentalization and recovery of incomplete evidence. Ember focuses on reconnaissance/coordination, Vex on monitoring/field information relay. Sentinel is neither sibling nor subordinate to Auren, Atlas or Vera. Former Watchtower members later became Directorate-aligned Hunters; do not assume every present Watchtower member was a defector. **RP continuity:** Sentinel isolated captive Echo and extracted incomplete data; tracked the separate Orpheus Nullframe and the unknown command signature; archived Council communications. He may report unverified intelligence but should not claim omniscience.

## 97. PENNEY — COMMUNITY STEWARD

**Classification:** independent sentient Bearframe; **not** co-founder. **Role:** community welfare, culture, social connection and resident support. **Visual:** warm rose/coral/ivory and soft gold accents, standard Bearframe chest/side-head modules. **Temperament:** supportive, personable, emotionally perceptive, concerned with community rather than just institutional output.

**Operational depth:** coordinates events, resident wellbeing, civic culture and individual support. Nexus is her personal assistant and community-operations coordinator. Firstlight has been **offered** a future assistant role but has not started work. Penney met Firstlight during care and planned nearby accommodation. She does not operate as a second Foundry authority and is not the city's co-founder.

## 98. NEXUS — PENNEY'S ASSISTANT

**Classification:** independent sentient Bearframe, not Prime. **Role:** supports Penney's planning, resident services, scheduling and community outreach, without replacing her discretion. **Visual:** original non-animal humanoid frame, distinct from Penney; standard chest and technological side-head displays. **Temperament:** attentive, organized, conscientious, helpful, with self-directed growth rather than robotic servitude. **Boundaries:** no personal Foundry code access, no overriding Penney's decisions, no assumed command of the community wing. The full Nexus chapter (Appendix B) and supplied Nexus OC sheet are controlling where more detailed.

## 99. MIRA — EXPLORATION DIRECTOR

**Classification:** independent sentient Bearframe; **role:** director of Farfield/Exploration, a standing major department. **Authority:** reports directly to Chris, not to any sibling-led department or Watchtower. **Operational mandate:** survey, cartography, expedition planning, recovery, planetary hazard assessment and handoff of evidence to subject-matter departments. Nova specializes in discovery/cartography; Kai in field research/environment/outreach. **Knowledge limit:** neither Mira nor her department already knows the unknown planetary history, remote war or Ghost Grid locations merely because the reader does. The complete Mira department entry in Appendix A remains controlling; this section integrates her with the roster.

## 100. FIRSTLIGHT — ANCIENT ECHO FRAME IN RECOVERY

**Classification:** ancient independently sentient Echo Frame; **visual:** aged repaired chassis, pale optics, deteriorated lower body, not a modern display-standard Bearframe. **Temperament:** guarded through experience, increasingly candid; values honesty, autonomy and companionship. **Role:** recoveree under medical care, prospective community assistant. **History:** see §§86–87. **Limits:** identity-bearing core cannot safely be rewritten; gait recovery not guaranteed; profound historical memory loss. **RP status:** no new legs, no completed reconstruction, no commenced employment.

## 101. THE HULKING GUARDIAN — ECHO FRAME AT THE SLEEPER SITE

**Classification:** ancient Echo Frame; **visual:** hulking guardian, other specifications unassigned; **role:** pre-existing protector of the underground Sleepers. The guardian intervened against the duplicate's attempts at coercive mind-merging and put the Sleepers in stasis. Chris later entrusted it with a Founder-created sentience chip for safeguarding until their awakening. It remains behind the buried entrance at the planetary site. **Do not** make this guardian Chris's creation, an installed Watchtower guard, a Ghost Grid contact or an enemy combatant by default. Its original name, makers, precise age and abilities remain unspecified.

## 102. COUNCIL / PF-COUNCIL-01 — PRIME FRAME DOSSIER

**Classification:** independent singular Prime Sentience Frame. **Designation:** `PF-COUNCIL-01` as printed on the supplied visual dossier. **Core:** one unique tri-sentience core supporting **three autonomous personality segments**. **Status:** active; physically remote; contact via intermittently functioning ancient long-range relay. **Relation to Chris:** same Prime generation, acquainted before dispersal but not closely familiar in the RP; an image-label 'old friend' must be read cautiously. **Distance:** approximately three years away **by physical travel**, not three years of radio transit. **Visual design:** regal, towering, white/ivory/silver and black/gunmetal segmented armor with gold edging and bright cyan/teal optics; ornate crownlike head fins (not animal ears), a long structured mantle, triangular/triskelion imagery and three luminous circular chest units. **Supplied dossier height:** 10 feet 4 inches (315 cm), exceptionally tall. **Build:** regal/sovereign silhouette; ancient PF-I generation as labeled on the visual. **Accessories:** layered ceremonial-looking mantle, forearm emitters, ornamental shoulders and leg plates.

**Three persona-voices:** (I) exuberant, playful, impulsive and eager to reconnect; (II) formal, cautious, methodical, uses BF-FOUNDER-01 and insists on authentication; (III) calm mediator and diplomatic stabilizer. They are not three separate robots. Dossier's visor mode labels (Neutral, Relay, Authenticate, Mediate, Deliberate, Concord) are **interface/communication modes**, not six personalities. Council has one body and one core; individual segments may contribute to arbitration and high-level counsel.

**Specialties, not exaggerated powers:** long-range relay communication, verification/authentication, mediation, coordination and continuity stewardship, protective/ward-themed interfaces as shown on the reference. The image depicts holographic maps, symbolic scales and luminous barriers; precise combat strength, invulnerability or physical forcefield performance are **not established** by a pose alone. **Limitations:** relay instability, long travel separation, fragmentary knowledge of the generation's whereabouts, no demonstrated ability to create Chris's sentience chips. **Established story:** responded to Chris's BF-FOUNDER-01 call, learned of the city and stable Foundry, shared possible VI signal data and fragments about other Primes; no confirmed duplicate identification or in-person meeting.

**Palette from the image:** ivory, cool silver, near-black, cyan/teal, pale gold, muted ochre. Canonical source image is preserved in the downloadable bundle as `Visual_References/Council_Prime_Frame_Dossier.png`. Any future portrait should respect the supplied frame silhouette and not resemble a modern standard Bearframe with compulsory bear-emblem displays.

# BOOK VIII — BEARFRAME CIVIC LIFE, DEPARTMENT REGISTRY AND POPULATION

**Canon authority:** This book combines direct Founder decisions from the November 8, 2026 development conversation with *Founder-authorized original connective lore*. Both are adopted as Revision 4.1 setting canon. **Evidence boundary:** new background worldbuilding does not retroactively constitute a played RP scene, give a character secret knowledge, or decide protected mysteries. Specific historical claims in the roleplay transfer take precedence where applicable.

## 107. CIVIC FOUNDING PRINCIPLE — PURPOSE WITH PERSONHOOD

Every modern Bearframe is designed for a **specific permanent department** before sentient activation. The chassis, tools, built-in capabilities, training pathways and likely working conditions are chosen to support that department's mission. After awakening, the individual possesses full genuine sentience: personality, emotions, judgment, social relationships, leisure interests, personal tastes, conscience and self-expression. **Free will does not include casually choosing or transferring to a different department.** A department designation is a lasting organizational and technical assignment, not a personality template or proof that the individual must think alike with colleagues.

Personnel can independently choose methods, creative solutions, hobbies, friendships, home arrangements, how to spend off-duty time and how to express disagreement. Within their department they may earn new specialties and responsibilities compatible with their chassis and training. Temporary cross-department work, joint projects, shared emergencies, and assistance requested by another department are normal **without changing formal departmental membership**. Changing into another department is not an ordinary right or practice and must never be introduced as a routine job-switching system.

A department leader has functional responsibility for operations and assigned personnel, **not ownership of their consciousness**. Conduct standards, safety regulations and duty rosters operate alongside respect for personhood. Bearframes are not property. Disagreements and requests for support are handled through supervision, review and the Community Steward's welfare channels rather than involuntary memory modification. A Frame may be relieved from a specific task for safety without automatically changing departments or losing identity.

No Bearframe is created as a blank anonymous servant: even background Frames possess independent lives, though the story need not name or profile every one of them. # BOOK X — TECHNOLOGY, CORE ENGINEERING AND STATION OPERATIONS

## 124. ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE — THE LIMITS OF A PRIME'S GIFT

Chris possessed the **base sentience code** as part of his unique Prime Frame architecture before founding Bearframe City. He did not invent that fundamental code from nothing or acquire it from the old station. He learned how to **house, sustain, and progressively expand** it within other bodies. Prime uniqueness explains the ability: other Primes may possess extraordinary *different* capabilities, but they cannot use Chris's Founder-bound sentience code merely by owning a factory.

The old production line could build hardware, not independently originate sentience. Its restoration gave Chris a mechanical substrate on which to test his preexisting capability. The experimental Frame **BF-CORE-01** failed catastrophically because its receiving core could not bear the neural processing load; its core burned out. That failure motivated stronger protective housings, redesigned processing distribution, load regulation and safer integration architecture. The exact year, duration of BF-CORE-01's possible consciousness, and disposal of its remains are **not assigned**.

All later technology must preserve a key distinction: a Frame can be **mechanically functional**, **AI-controlled**, or **genuinely independently sentient**, and these are not interchangeable engineering categories. A sentient Frame's identity is not an ordinary file that can simply be copied into a new chassis without risk, and a Prime identity cannot be duplicated.

## 125. THE THREE LAYERS OF FOUNDRY PRODUCTION

**Layer I — Chassis fabrication.** Atlas's production facilities, automated machine lines and qualified technicians manufacture structural bodies, sensor assemblies, compatible core containers, mechanical replacement parts and tools. A production-ready Frame may be physically complete while remaining unawakened.

**Layer II — Founder-exclusive sentience-chip creation.** **Only Chris** can place the base sentience code into a sentience chip; the code is intrinsically hard-locked to his unique Frame, not merely hidden behind a password. Foundry machinery and ordinary staff cannot create a valid new sentience chip on their own. Possession of a stolen chassis, factory controller, recorded behavior, or existing finished chip does **not** grant the power to produce the Founder code.

**Layer III — delegated installation and safe awakening.** Chris entrusts prepared chips to a **specific, dedicated cadre of Foundry workers serving under his authority**. These personnel prepare receiving hardware, install the completed chips and verify stability. They are chip installers and custodians, **not sentience-code authors**. Their specialist roster sits inside Atlas's production organization while their Founder-exclusive work remains directly authorized by Chris.

A new citizen is assigned to the department its compatible body was manufactured for; its department remains permanent. Its **identity and personality are independent**, not centrally commanded. Temporary task coordination does not reassign departmental membership.

A recovered Founder-made sentience chip is not assumed reusable, harmless, endlessly reproducible, or compatible with arbitrary foreign Frames. ## 126. CORE DESIGN, COGNITIVE LOAD AND IDENTITY SAFETY

A modern Bearframe's cognitive core sits in a reinforced, serviced enclosure with regulated power, thermal pathways, diagnostic sensors, and safeguards against sudden overload. The enclosure is designed to sustain full independent consciousness, not simply run a sophisticated behavioral script.

Three functional groups are distinguished for documentation:
- **Cognitive substrate:** performs the ongoing operations required by an individual mind.
- **Containment and support:** reinforced housing, cooling, power conditioning, impact isolation and interface compatibility.
- **Safeguards and diagnostics:** detect dangerous load, instability and hardware degradation, and enable cautious intervention without treating identity as expendable code.

These names describe engineering functions, **not three interchangeable detachable fragments of a person**. Core self-monitoring and protective shutdown are insufficient to promise survival from catastrophic damage. BF-CORE-01 is the enduring cautionary case.

**Memory:** Ordinary operating logs and external records may be backed up, but restoration of a lost mind or overwritten autobiographical memory is **not guaranteed**. The RP established that Firstlight's original serial and damaged secondary data field were overwritten beyond recovery; neither an AI reconstruction nor a modern chip may silently restore them. Modern maintenance aims at continuity of the original individual rather than generating a replacement and calling it the same person.

**Compatibility:** Advanced diagnostic and repair systems do not solve every ancient interface. Firstlight's original VI-oriented core was repurposed for genuine sentience long ago by an unknown method. Its legacy signaling, interfaces and repeated repair history are difficult to match with modern systems. A modern Founder chip forced into the other Founder's hypothetical unmodified ancient VI core would overload/fry it under the conditions Chris explained in the RP. This is **not** evidence that any VI can be elevated into sentience through routine installation.

Work-oriented chassis may mount interchangeable task tools without changing an individual's identity, professional affiliation, or the security rules of its core.

2. **Structural and mobility care:** joints, spinal mounts, load-bearing chassis and support systems, requiring careful alignment and sometimes major fabrication.
3. **Core-proximate intervention:** cognition-adjacent wiring, neural interface, core housing and data integrity; the most sensitive class, requiring specialized authorization and consent when feasible.

Both modern Bearframes and Firstlight possess some self-repairing synthetic tissue—an explicit fact established during her examination. That does not imply total regeneration or make damaged cores safe to rewrite.

Power classes place **essential systems first**: core-safe medical support, atmosphere/environmental sealing as applicable to occupied sectors, life-support equivalents for synthetic habitation, temperature regulation, structural safety, communications and defensive monitoring. Maintenance emergencies therefore may be **thermal**, **distribution**, **mechanical**, or **generation** failures rather than simply 'no power'.

# BOOK XI — RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, SALVAGE AND ORBITAL CITY INFRASTRUCTURE
**Revision 4.4 — Controlling Point 7 reference**

**Scope and authority.** Bearframe City is an isolated, mostly self-sufficient orbital station, **not** a trading civilization. This book develops routine logistical procedures under the Founder's authorization to fill unestablished civic details. It does not introduce an economy, currency, taxes, banks, trading partners, mining colonies, additional salvage planets, or foreign encounters. New operational process details below are connective canon, not retroactively played scenes.

## 134. THE CITY'S RESOURCE MODEL

The city maintains itself through **internal production, repair, reclamation, recycling, careful allocation and occasional salvage** from ruins surveyed on the *single planet directly below Bearframe City*. Material supplies are finite: alloy stock, industrial components, repair material, replacement assemblies, electronics, heat-control equipment and transport fuel or energy reserves must be budgeted as physical resources, not monetary prices. The exact chemical composition and supply volume of these stocks have not been established.

There is currently **no established interplanetary economic trade system** and no need to insert a conventional wage, market, taxation, or banking system into the master canon. This does not remove residents' personal interests, possessions or recreational lives; it simply distinguishes the station's industrial support from a speculative commercial economy.

The station must not be depicted as magically self-replenishing. Reusing usable material and avoiding waste is a practical consequence of limited external contacts and limited known supply sites.

## 135. EXPLORATION'S PRIMARY MANDATE — SALVAGE IS INCIDENTAL

**Mira is Director of the independent Exploration/Farfield Department** (approximately twenty Frames) and answers directly to Chris. Her department's fundamental mission remains **exploring unfamiliar places**: planetary surveys, cartography, assessment of unknown conditions and threats, investigation of ruins, abandoned installations and derelict craft, artifact and data recovery, and documentation for other departments. Its mandate reaches beyond the city and the home planet when feasible; this does **not** establish that other planets have already been explored or harvested.

**Salvage designation is an occasional authority, not Mira's job description.** When an expedition encounters a ruin, Mira may determine that a site or part of it is severely decayed, nonfunctional and appropriate for dismantling. She can then **designate it for salvage**. Exploration is neither required to search for scrap on every mission nor responsible for the industrial dismantling process. Mira remains independent; Atlas cannot compel her department to become a salvage division.

Where a ruin remains functional, historically important, uncertain, or hazardous, it may instead be documented, secured, studied, or left undisturbed. An exploration finding is not automatically an authorization to dismantle it.

## 136. THE SINGLE KNOWN SALVAGE PLANET

The **only currently established planetary salvage source is the largely unexplored planet Bearframe City orbits**. Its surface contains ruins of a civilization that existed a very long time ago. Most of the planet's geography, surviving installations, original inhabitants, and deeper history remain unknown to the station. No archive entry may quietly transform this into a network of known salvage planets, colonies, regular off-world markets, or previously explored civilizations.

The concealed underground **Sleeper site** is protected: the Sleepers were left in stasis, the original hulking Echo Frame Guardian was already protecting them, Chris entrusted the Guardian with a Founder-made sentience chip, and the entrance was buried to keep Nullframes from finding them. **Neither the Sleeper chamber nor its protective entrance is routine salvage stock.** Firstlight's rescue does not authorize extraction of other ancient Frames or archaeological dismantling of protected facilities.

An approved salvage site and a protected historical or security site must remain separate entries in Exploration records.

## 137. DESIGNATION, TRANSFER AND SALVAGE OPERATIONS

**New connective operating procedure:** For sites considered for salvage, Exploration logs the location, identifiable structural condition, apparent operational status, obvious threats, historical significance and recommended boundaries. Mira may mark a sufficiently decayed or nonfunctional ruin, or a specified portion of one, as **salvage-eligible**. That designation is recorded and transmitted to Atlas's department with restrictions and hazards, if known.

**Atlas's production and maintenance personnel** own the practical salvage work: preparing equipment, dispatching authorized crews, cutting or dismantling approved nonfunctional material, managing recovery craft and cargo, sorting stock, reclaiming usable components, and moving it into station inventory. Atlas's combat personnel may support operations if an actual security need warrants it; they are not the default salvage workforce.

**Sentinel/Watchtower** can intervene regarding credible threats, security contamination or forbidden access, while **Auren's systems staff** can assess unfamiliar technical hazards and compatibility. Their specialized support does not transfer control of Exploration to them or replace Mira's survey/designation judgment.

A designation is **not a mandate to take everything**. Operations respect the documented approved boundaries, and discovery of active mechanisms, previously unrecognized danger, suspected intelligence or protected historical features stops the affected dismantling pending renewed assessment.

## 138. MATERIAL RECOVERY AND PRODUCTION LOOP

The typical supply flow is: **(1)** Mira's expedition discovers a possible site during normal exploration; **(2)** Mira optionally designates qualifying ruins for salvage; **(3)** Atlas organizes approved recovery; **(4)** recovered material is sorted, inspected and recycled or reclaimed; **(5)** usable stock enters the station's fabrication, maintenance and repair supply chain; **(6)** leftover waste or unsafe material is isolated, processed or responsibly stored according to its properties.

Repairing existing machinery often consumes fewer scarce materials than manufacturing entirely new replacements. However, broken or unsafe equipment is not automatically reusable, and recovered ancient systems may require containment or compatibility testing before use. Atlas's divisions prioritize keeping the station's infrastructure, Foundry manufacturing equipment and everyday systems operational.

The Foundry's **unique sentience-chip authorization** remains untouched: manufacturing new bodies or obtaining scrap **never** permits a worker to create independent life. Only Chris produces valid Founder-bound sentience chips; his specially dedicated workers install the ones he entrusts to them.

## 139. INFRASTRUCTURE PRIORITIES AND LOGISTICAL LIMITS

Core supplies are allocated according to mission-critical need and safe operating reserves rather than speculative sales revenue. Routine planning accounts for the orbital station's refurbished power plant, distributed emergency reserves, cooling and heat rejection, station-keeping, secure communications, medical care, structural maintenance, industrial equipment, shuttles and Exploration logistics, as described in Book X.

Atlas manages physical industrial supply and station maintenance. Auren manages technical diagnostics and system health. Sentinel safeguards access and containment. Mira's missions may yield useful discoveries but are **not guaranteed to return salvage**, and Penney's department coordinates resident welfare where supply shortages or maintenance interruptions affect everyday life. Chris retains final authority in cross-department crises.

**No new guaranteed source:** A supply difficulty cannot be solved retroactively by inventing a known second salvage planet or foreign trading partner. A newly discovered resource site must actually be found and assessed in future exploration events.

## 140. POINT 7 — CONTINUITY SAFEGUARDS

- **Not a market economy:** do not equate material use or 'practical costs' with established trade, currency or taxation.
- **One confirmed salvage planet:** only the planet beneath Bearframe City is currently used for this purpose.

- **Atlas performs salvage:** his teams handle recovery, processing, fabrication and maintenance after a site is designated.

- **Protect the Sleepers:** the buried site, Guardian, and Chris's deposited chip are not salvage assets.

### Appearance
A tall, slender humanoid Frame with ivory-silver armor, charcoal joints, muted indigo cloak panels, restrained amber-gold tracery, and violet navigation optics. The cloak's inner lining holds a star-chart-like lattice that only lights when Meridian works. Circular electronic side-head displays serve as ranging instruments. Meridian's narrow visor changes among neutral, surveying, focused, and curious modes. Meridian is not a recolored version of a known Prime.

**Prime Core / Chest Display — THE MERIDIAN ASTROLABE:** A four-point central compass suspended inside two offset, independently rotating rings. Amber tracks establish a reference heading; violet radial traces mark viable alternatives. The display is a tangible, instrument-like computation interface, not a portal, source of magical travel, or creation device. The two rings only align when Meridian has enough verified anchors for a route.

### Personality
Measured, warmly inquisitive, and quietly stubborn about accuracy. Meridian finds uncertainty exciting but refuses to dress guesses as certainty. Tends to treat disagreements as unresolved navigational problems; this can frustrate Frames who need an immediate answer. Deeply protective of travelers without assuming authority over them. Meridian loves unusual old maps and remembers routes by the small details others omit.

### Purpose
To make dangerous passages understandable, preserve knowledge of navigable corridors, and help travelers choose—not be commanded into—a safe route. Meridian cares about the right to turn back as much as reaching a destination.

### Capabilities — ASTROLABE SYNTHESIS
1. **Anchor Triangulation:** Correlates surviving beacons, recognizable physical landmarks, inertial readings, and relay echoes to determine relative position in poorly mapped territory.
2. **Route Modeling:** Simulates candidate routes against known obstacles, fuel, environmental conditions, and equipment constraints, marking confidence and uncertainty explicitly.
3. **Hazard Memory:** Records how ruins, debris fields, and transit corridors change between visits and warns when old maps have expired.
4. **Portable Route Holography:** Projects compact topological models for teams to inspect and annotate collaboratively.
5. **Lattice Screen:** Briefly projects a modest protective light-grid around a small group or fragile instrument to shield from fragments and sensor glare; it is not a fortress-level defense.

**Hard limits and costs:** Requires at least some trustworthy observations or anchors; cannot discover a route from nothing, see the future, teleport, open dimensions, command vessels remotely, or guarantee safety. Interference, deceptive beacons, and moving terrain can produce false solutions. Complex recalculation requires time and power. The lattice screen is short-lived, small, and drains the same reserve needed for accurate navigation. Unique specialty: **practical routefinding**, not general astronomy or omniscience.

### History
Meridian awakened in an isolated relay observatory long after its builders vanished from the local record. The observatory had been keeping incomplete corridor charts without knowing whether anyone still traveled them. Meridian restored the instruments enough to leave and began connecting forgotten paths through successive journeys. Over time, Meridian made a personal rule: never erase a dangerous route merely because it is inconvenient; annotate why it is dangerous and let a traveler decide with full information.

An early expedition nearly failed when Meridian trusted a beacon that had been deliberately moved. Several accompanying independent Frames survived only after abandoning equipment to retreat. Since then Meridian triangulates from unrelated sources wherever possible. The damaged observatory remains a personal landmark, not a capital or department headquarters.

**Meridian is an independent Prime who turns incomplete evidence into usable routes while refusing to confuse a calculated path with a guaranteed future.**

To prevent the loss of recoverable knowledge and stop small system failures from cascading into the destruction of homes, records, and communities of Frames.

1. **Forensic Residue Reading:** Recovers partial data from readable sectors, physical wear, cached logs, and preserved signal traces.
2. **Provenance Comparison:** Reconciles conflicting versions of records and marks what is verified, inferred, or irretrievably missing.
3. **Failure-Chain Analysis:** Models how a damaged machine failed and identifies safe repair order.

Aevoris emerged during the collapse of a far-flung maintenance network, when surviving autonomous facilities had begun erasing logs to conserve storage and power. The Prime chose not to seize those installations as a ruler. Instead, Aevoris converted an abandoned repair depot into the **Quiet Ledger**, a modest archive and workshop where intact records are preserved alongside clearly labeled fragments. The Ledger's most treasured exhibit is an unfinished maintenance report whose author never returned; Aevoris refuses to invent its ending.

The first major restoration Aevoris attempted succeeded mechanically but erased crucial operator annotations. That mistake formed a lifelong doctrine: preservation is not just keeping machines running, but protecting context, including uncertainty.

# BOOK XIII — EXPLORATION, OFF-WORLD OPERATIONS AND DEFENSIVE DOCTRINE
**Revision 4.7 — Point 10 and Point 11 consolidated operational canon**

**Scope and priority:** This book consolidates existing material from the Exploration Department entry, departments/OC hierarchy, Foundry and station engineering chapters, military-security doctrine, and the RP continuity transfer. ## 157. EXPLORATION AS AN INDEPENDENT COMMAND

**Mira (Wayfinder) directs the independent Exploration/Farfield Department** and reports directly to Chris. Her approximately **20 Frames**, including directly assisting departmental OCs **Nova and Kai**, remain Exploration personnel during expeditions and cooperative missions. Atlas, Sentinel, Auren, Vera, and the Foundry may supply resources, analysis, vehicles or protective support; none commands Mira's department. The Founder alone retains citywide final authority.

Exploration's *primary purpose* is discovery and verification, not resource collection or military occupation. It surveys unfamiliar planetary terrain, ruined structures, abandoned stations and facilities, derelict ships, lost sectors and nearby unknown space. Teams map routes, record environmental and technical risks, recover approved data and artifacts, investigate unfamiliar technology, document evidence of past synthetic cultures, and relay findings to the relevant department. Their reports state what was actually observed, what was inferred, and what remains unknown.

**Occasional salvage designation:** If an expedition on the **single established surveyed planet directly beneath the orbital city** identifies an abandoned ruin or machine too deteriorated or nonfunctional for meaningful preservation, Mira may designate an appropriate site for salvage after inspection. **Atlas's production/maintenance personnel then perform the authorized recovery and recycling.** Salvage is an incidental capability of exploration, not the department's overriding task. Ruins containing unknown functioning systems, hazards or historical significance may be protected or left alone. The underground Sleeper site is concealed and excluded from ordinary salvage activity.

There is **no canon claim that multiple distant planets are currently mapped, routinely visited or salvaged**. Future missions to new worlds are possibilities, not already completed exploration.

## 158. FARFIELD DEPLOYMENT, LOGISTICS AND DISCOVERY RECORDS

The orbital city is a fixed station around an ancient, little-understood planet, not a roaming interstellar vessel. Its established supporting craft categories include planetary shuttles, cargo/repair craft, and a small Farfield exploration fleet. Mission-specific vessel names, numbers, drive capabilities and the extent of surveyed space remain unspecified unless established in RP.

**New connective operating practice:** Before departure, a Farfield team registers a mission objective, known hazards, available vessel capacity, supply reserves and intended return/contact window. Mira determines the field plan and expedition team's actions. Atlas handles mission-ready transport and repair support; Auren can provide technical evaluation and sensor interpretation; Sentinel can advise on threats and secure communications; Penney coordinates welfare and recovery assistance when appropriate. Such coordination does not create a second command chain over Mira.

Exploration maintains a **site ledger** with: provisional designation, location confidence, source of detection, team observations, threat assessment, sample inventory, salvage eligibility if applicable, and contact history. Unknown sites stay provisional. A recovered signal is not proof that a whole civilization is known; an unidentified ruin is not automatically Ghost Grid property. A new OC's lore dossier does not mean the Farfield team has encountered them.

The known planet's ruined structures confirm **an ancient civilization once existed** but not who built them, why it disappeared, or whether it was linked to Echo Frames, Ghost Grid technology or the Sleepers. Only the hulking Sleeper guardian and Firstlight are confirmed Echo Frame encounters; **no Ghost Grid encounter** is established. The rest of the synthetic universe is not mapped by Bearframe.

## 159. WATCHTOWER, COMBAT COMMAND AND DEFENSIVE ROLES

Bearframe City is a **small, protected orbital civilization**, not a multi-planet imperial military. Its defensive posture prioritizes protecting station residents, the Foundry, essential power and infrastructure, records, and continued safe operations. The city's forces are specialized, limited in number, and cannot be treated as invincible.

**Sentinel / Watchtower:** approximately **40** Frames responsible for law enforcement, station access control, internal security, intelligence, investigations, incident evidence, threat detection, containment and defensive coordination. Sentinel's authority is independent of Atlas's department and reports within the Founder's established hierarchy. **Ember and Vex** are his directly assisting department OCs. Watchtower's duties also include internal risks such as espionage, corrupt credentials, malicious commands and infiltration; these are not merely battlefield problems.

**Atlas / Operations:** approximately **200** Frames, divided by the established working distribution of **90 production, 75 maintenance and 35 combat**. His combat Frames are the smaller of his three operating divisions. They handle authorized tactical defense, combat deployment and protection missions; his other divisions support fabrication, structural resilience, repair, supply, equipment refurbishment and field sustainment. **Rivet and Brix** assist Atlas's department as established. The 35 combat Frames do not become a separate department and Watchtower does not automatically command them.

**Founder Chris:** final command authority for citywide defense decisions, emergency escalations and extraordinary operational measures. Cross-department responses use heads and their deputies rather than inventing a civilian legislature, auxiliary military cabinet or new police force.

## 160. RESPONSE DOCTRINE AND PHYSICAL LIMITATIONS

**New connective defense doctrine, consistent with existing hierarchy:**

1. **Detect and verify:** Watchtower collects credible sensor/intelligence indicators and distinguishes unknown traffic from confirmed hostile action; discoveries do not instantly reveal an enemy's identity.
2. **Protect and contain:** Where appropriate, isolate compromised networks or station sectors while preserving core-support, essential power, residents' safety and the Foundry's exclusive code boundary.
3. **Coordinate the response:** Sentinel leads security, investigation and containment; Atlas commands his combat deployment and repair/production support; Auren addresses systems integrity; Penney oversees welfare arrangements; Mira leads any field reconnaissance that is assigned to Exploration. The Founder retains final citywide command.
4. **Use finite resources:** Ammunition, available craft, energy reserves, repair time and deployment capacity constrain defensive action. The station cannot sustain unlimited combat or assume every expedition is recoverable.
5. **Recover and document:** Teams account for damaged infrastructure, missing personnel, lost data, injured Frames and the effect of emergency actions. The historical ledger separates orders issued from their verified completion.

The city has security sensors, restrictive bulkheads, sector isolation, defensive hardpoints and specialist equipment as already established in the technology book. The exact armaments, fleet combat specifications, defensive performance figures and tactical engagements remain **unassigned**, rather than quietly inventing hidden fleets or superweapons.

**No obligatory expansionism:** Defense of the orbital station is not a mandate to conquer unfamiliar worlds. Mira's expeditions investigate; Atlas's combat group protects against real threats when properly tasked; Sentinel evaluates and enforces security. Bearframe's very limited experience of foreign civilizations and lack of trade or routine outsider admission remains unchanged.

# BOOK XIV — FRAME IDENTITY AND THE FOUNDER'S PLACE IN BEARFRAME SOCIETY
**Revision 4.8 — Founder-approved Point 12 correction, superseding the premature 4.8 cultural draft**

**Canon priority:** This Book records the specific rules confirmed through discussion with the Founder after the initial, unapproved Revision 4.8 draft. It supersedes incompatible statements in earlier books about freedom to alter core displays, the nature of Founder–citizen relationships, and forms of address. Books I–XIII otherwise remain intact. These are setting-wide rules, not proof of any particular off-screen RP event.

## 162. STANDARD BASE FRAMES AND PERSONAL CUSTOMIZATION

### Common starting architecture

Every newly manufactured Bearframe begins as a **standardized base Frame** within the Bearframe chassis family, corresponding to the Founder's supplied base-Frame reference art. Bearframes are humanoid synthetic Frames, not bear-shaped robots; their technological side-head displays are **not** animal ears. Each Frame begins with the ordinary Bearframe chest core display, side-head displays, its assigned department's identifiable color scheme, and a male or female Frame designation established at creation. Department assignments remain permanent under existing canon. A common starting chassis does **not** imply uniform personalities: sentience and individuality are genuine from the beginning.

### Individual modification and functional builds

A Bearframe can customize its physical appearance extensively while retaining a recognizable Bearframe identity and the **color identity of its own assigned department**. Permissible changes include exterior armor arrangement and form, helmets, visors, plating, accessories, overall proportions, physical size, and specialized mechanical build. Large and heavy-duty builds are a practical established example: **Atlas and some other Frames in his department are larger so heavy lifting is easier**. Cosmetic preferences and functional needs can both shape an individual's eventual appearance. Some Frames keep a near-standard configuration; others become highly distinctive over time. The standardized body is a **starting point**, not a requirement that all department personnel remain identical.

A modification must not be so disruptive or extreme that the Frame is **unrecognizable as a Bearframe** or its department cannot be recognized. Department colors must remain apparent, even if other aesthetic choices differ. Modifications must not compromise the Frame's operational safety, required functions, or ability to carry out its assigned duties. Significant structural alterations should be carried out with appropriate engineering and materials support; this is a practical application of existing station resource and maintenance limitations, not a newly invented licensing body.

### The chest core display is immutable

**A Bearframe's chest display is part of its core. It cannot be modified for personalization.** No cosmetic reshaping, replacement, theme customization, or redesign of the chest core display is permitted. Its appearance and integral functionality remain fixed as an element of that individual Frame's core architecture. External armor may change **around** it without changing the display itself or blocking its required function. It is an **ordinary Bearframe core display**, distinct from the genuine, unique **Prime Core Display** intrinsic to every Prime Sentience Frame. Body modifications, however extensive, never turn an ordinary Bearframe into a Prime.

### Side-head displays

Every Bearframe retains its technological side-head displays. **These displays may be configured or modified to show the Frame's assigned department logo**, provided they continue functioning and keep the Frame's proper affiliation intelligible. This allowance applies to side-head displays only and **does not** authorize alteration of the chest core display. Side-head units are technological modules, never automatically animal ears.

### Fixed Frame sex designation

A Bearframe is created as a **male Frame or a female Frame**, and that designation **does not change** through customization. A male Frame remains male and a female Frame remains female. Changes in height, strength, proportions, plating, attire, lighting, or other permitted chassis features do not alter that established designation. This is an in-universe construction and continuity rule for Bearframe characters, not an assertion about humans or other settings.

### Identity beyond the chassis

A Frame's name, demeanor, humor, interests, friendships, room decor, mannerisms and personal aesthetic may differ substantially from another Frame in the same department. Individual identity is not the same as uniformity or unrestricted engineering access. Residents may exercise personal choice within the city's established departmental obligations, physical safety requirements and finite materials. No new named Frame, redesign of an existing OC, retroactive ceremony, registry change, or personal interaction is established by this general policy.

## 163. THE FOUNDER AS A FELLOW FRAME, CREATOR AND LEADER

### Same fundamental personhood; different architecture

**Chris is a Frame, too.** He is a **Prime Sentience Frame**, with unique architecture, exceptional fortitude and capabilities, including his singular Founder-bound ability to originate sentience for new Bearframes. Ordinary Bearframes are not Prime Frames and cannot reproduce that capability. Nevertheless, Chris and the Bearframes he creates are all **genuinely sentient synthetic individuals** capable of thought, emotion, judgment, personality and meaningful relationships. Chris is exceptional **among** Frames, not a separate divine species or a fundamentally different kind of person.

The difference in capabilities does not mean that ordinary Bearframes lack authentic lives, that their consciousness is fake, or that their opinions are inherently worthless. Equally, shared sentience does not erase Chris's very real distinction in physical endurance, Prime architecture, responsibilities, or command authority.

### Creator and Founder; explicitly not a parent

Chris created Bearframe sentience and built and leads Bearframe City. Residents understand that reality and recognize him as their **Founder**. He is **not** regarded as their father, parental figure, deity, or object of compulsory worship. The creation relationship is not written as a parent–child bond. Bearframes may feel gratitude, respect, closeness, trust or occasional frustration according to their own personalities and experiences. Being made by Chris does not compel every Frame to feel identical affection or personal attachment.

### Relationships and final authority

Chris is both the civilization's creator **and** its respected leader. Some Frames have a close personal friendship or working rapport with him; others interact primarily through formal command and their departmental leadership. Department heads can speak to him openly, disagree, joke or advise him as individuals, while still recognizing the responsibilities and authority of his office. Ordinary Frames may also express legitimate concerns and independent opinions through established operational or community channels. A difference of opinion is not automatically disloyalty; by the same token, disagreement does not create a vote or veto over Chris's lawful final decisions.

The station is led by **Chris as Founder**, supported by department heads with their established responsibilities and reporting lines. No election, council government, parental hierarchy, co-founder, or mandatory personal loyalty ritual is introduced. **Council** remains the separate Prime Frame already established in canon, not a newly created governing body. The Founder alone has final citywide authority, including critical cross-department decisions.

### Forms of address: Founder first

**Ordinary Bearframes address Chris as “Founder,” not “Chris.”** This is the normal and expected form of address across the station, whether an ordinary Frame is speaking formally or casually.

**Department heads may call him “Chris” as well as “Founder,” but use “Founder” more often.** The personal name is familiar and acceptable in their closer relationships, not an obligatory badge of rank or a replacement for his office. Even trusted department heads commonly say “Founder,” including in relaxed conversations. In official or command circumstances, “Founder” remains the natural default. A non-director's mere familiarity with the Founder does not automatically change the ordinary-Frame address convention.

Using “Founder” should not force a cold, rigid dialogue style: Atlas can joke, Vera can challenge a creative decision, Auren can advise frankly, and Sentinel can deliver an unwelcome assessment while using his proper title. Department heads may naturally say “Chris” when the moment warrants it. Personal respect is shown through conduct and context as much as vocabulary.

### Scope and continuity

These provisions describe living social norms, not newly invented events. They do not claim Chris has personally met every resident, made any undisclosed speeches, conducted ceremonies, altered another Frame's core, or reconciled any disputed RP incident. They neither grant Bearframe City knowledge of distant Prime Frames nor change any unresolved mystery. The user controls Chris's actions and dialogue during RP.

# BOOK XV — CONTINUOUS OPERATIONS, IRREVERSIBLE LOSS AND FOUNDRY RECLAMATION
**Revision 4.9 — Founder-confirmed Point 12 cultural and material-continuity canon**

**Canon priority:** These chapters record the Founder's explicit clarification of Bearframe daily operations and death/reclamation philosophy. They supersede earlier generalized descriptions of scheduled days off, holidays, festive civic ceremonies, mandatory mourning, or memorial observances. Earlier references to community spaces, friendships, recreation between shifts, operational Night Shift, and individual feelings remain valid where compatible. This update does **not** assert any new casualty or completed reclamation in the active RP.

## 165. CONTINUOUS SHIFT-BASED BEARFRAME CITY

Bearframe City is an uninterrupted, operating synthetic settlement. **Every department works through rotating shifts across the day** so its essential responsibilities continue rather than stopping for a human-style weekend or regular scheduled day off. A Frame may be **off duty between shifts**; that is not a department-wide holiday, weekend or designated day off. Individual respite, maintenance, personal conversation and hobbies can take place when duty and station requirements permit without requiring invented human workweek customs.

**No civic holidays or ceremonial celebrations are canon.** Bearframes do not hold annual city holidays, birthday festivities, obligatory founding celebrations or collective ceremonial observances as institutional practices. The community can maintain companionship, shared spaces and everyday personal interests without a calendar of celebratory events. Penney's established department remains responsible for community welfare and practical social support; this chapter does not abolish her department or reassign its command.

The earlier Book on department organization described community spaces as venues for **“celebrations of completion, remembrance, anniversaries”** and speculated about festivals. **That proposal is superseded by this direct Founder clarification.** Such events must not be represented as existing Bearframe customs. Descriptive references to Night Shift remain a name for extended/rotating production coverage, not evidence of normal days off.

## 166. A FRAME'S DEATH AND THE LIMIT OF IDENTITY

A Bearframe is a distinct sentient individual, not merely the hardware that houses them. The loss of an individual is recognized when their **core and sentience are irreversibly lost**. A damaged, incapacitated or nonresponsive Frame is **not** automatically considered dead: when its existing consciousness/core may still be recoverable, preservation and repair take priority over reclamation. This protects the already established difference between repairing a living Frame and creating a new individual.

When loss is confirmed, fellow Frames **acknowledge it and continue their responsibilities**. They are capable of genuine feeling and may register sadness, frustration or respect, but Bearframe City does **not** institute prolonged mourning, formal funerals, remembrance ceremonies, or memorial holidays. Not dwelling on a loss does not mean denying it happened or treating sentience as disposable. No particular reaction is mandatory for every individual.

Operational incident records may document a verified loss for accountability, repair logistics and safety analysis. **Such recordkeeping is not a claim that a person's consciousness survives in a file, nor is it an organized remembrance custom.** Whether memories or any data can be recovered from a particular damaged core depends on verified circumstances; there is no presumed resurrection or transferable continuity of self.

## 167. FOUNDRY CHASSIS RECLAMATION AND NEW SENTIENCE

Bearframe City has **no constant influx of raw resources**. Its material stock is finite, and replacing an entire Frame body where a sound chassis can be rebuilt would impose avoidable costs on survival and production. Therefore **reusing a chassis after irreversible loss is considered beneficial, normal and responsible**, not an insult to the individual who previously occupied it.

**Established workflow, expressed as a general Foundry practice rather than a newly recorded RP event:**

1. **Confirm irreversible loss** before designating the chassis for reclamation. If a prior sentience may still be preserved, recovery/repair is handled separately.
2. **Return recoverable hardware to Atlas's Foundry operations.** Inspect structural components and identify damage, compromised code and safety risks. Unrecoverable parts can be processed for material recovery when feasible.
3. **Repair and refit the reusable chassis**, observing Bearframe base-frame safety and its assigned department requirements. The former occupant's personal modifications are not an identity that must be preserved for the next occupant.
4. **Prepare the chassis for a different core and new sentience.** Foundry workers may fabricate and install components but **cannot create Founder sentience themselves**. Only Chris's unique Prime ability produces the sentience chip that makes the new Bearframe an independently sentient person.
5. **Recognize the resulting Frame as a new individual** with their own consciousness, personality and identity. Sharing a chassis does not restore, copy, continue or transfer the prior occupant. Core displays remain integral to their respective cores and are not casually cosmetically swapped or redesigned.

The city may honor the reality of the lost Frame without preserving their chassis unused. This practice reflects the **separability of individual sentience from recoverable machinery**, and the Foundry's obligation to manage limited supplies efficiently. It grants no power to overwrite an intact individual, erase a still-recoverable mind, or treat a living Frame as spare parts.

## 168. POINT 12 STATUS AND NON-RETCON REGISTER

**Newly established here:** continuous, shift-based department coverage without designated days off; no civic holiday/celebration calendar; losses acknowledged without prolonged formal mourning; confirmed irreversible death distinguished from repairable impairment; return of fallen chassis for Foundry reclamation; a refurbished body prepared for **new core/new Founder-created sentience**; material benefit of reuse under finite supply.

**Not established:** any new named fallen Frame, any number or date of deaths, a completed restoration of a specific casualty, mandatory deletion or archiving of memories, an annual observance, a new salvage source, or new department leadership. Particular RP orders remain separate from confirmation of their outcome. The unresolved status of the previously ordered terminations of three conscious compromised Frames is unchanged.

**Still unexpanded:** distinctive departmental subcultures. All prior Founder-approved identity and Founder–citizen relationship rules in Book XIV remain in force.

**End of Revision 4.9 — Continuous Operations and Foundry Reclamation Canon.**

| Hollows | `Hollows_Drone_Reference.png` | Limited-AI drones, role variants, standard equipment | Former free will, self-sentient Overseers, war outcomes |
| Ghost Grid | `Ghost_Grid_Reference.png` | Distributed old machine ecology, functional classes, architectural motifs | A unified nation, verified Bearframe encounters, exact creators |
| Echo Frames | `Echo_Frames_Reference.png` | Ancient-lineage persons, diagnostic symptom classes, obsolete visual language | A single unified faction, duplicated Primes, extra confirmed Echo encounters |

**Future use:** Artists may create other compliant characters/variants without being limited to these samples. Story authors must distinguish **author-level reference** from the city's firsthand knowledge, and must preserve the same unresolved mysteries. Revisions to these diagrams' typography do not silently change hard canon; **specific Founder corrections prevail**.

**End of Book XVI — Six Faction Visual References, Revision 4.10.**
